title: Claims Service Standard on Claim Lag and Retroactive Points (Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements)
content:
**Standard.** For a retroactive points claim on a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement, the claim lag is the number of calendar days from the date the claimed ticket closed as flown — the date its record in Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand shows the ticket reaching flown — to the claim date. The claim lag decides how the shared claim points, the claim points at the last step before they are credited, are settled:

- **Lag of 21 calendar days or more:** the shared claim points are divided by 2 and rounded down to the whole point.
- **Lag of 8 calendar days or more, and fewer than 21:** they are multiplied by 0.75 and rounded up to the whole point.
- **Lag of fewer than 8 calendar days:** they are credited as they stand.

The settled claim points are the points credited for the retroactive claim.

### Settlement on hypothetical shared claim points of 483

| Claim lag | Settlement | Points credited |
|---|---|---|
| 30 days | 483 divided by 2 is 241.5, rounded down | 241 |
| 21 days | same | 241 |
| 20 days | 483 multiplied by 0.75 is 362.25, rounded up | 363 |
| 8 days | same | 363 |
| 7 days | as they stand | 483 |

### Counting the lag (hypothetical dates)

A ticket that closed as flown on 3 June and is claimed on 24 June has a lag of 21 days; claimed on 23 June, 20 days; claimed on 11 June, 8 days; claimed on 10 June, 7 days.
